page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Lasv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 1920 GB of local storage. The instance is Premium Storage capable but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring 3078.28 and Geekbench single-core scoring 2080.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates strong performance at 2723.0. In contrast, multi-core and memory benchmarks generally fall within the average range, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 12313.93 and a Passmark CPU score of 14433.95. A notable performance bottleneck is observed in memory bandwidth for large blocks, where read-only uncached operations score a weak 38.85 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25%. However, write bandwidth for large blocks remains average at 28.06 GB/sec, and cached small-block read bandwidth averages 607.39 GB/sec.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the 1920 GB of bundled local storage, this instance provides a high resource density suitable for memory-intensive and storage-centric workloads. The strong single-core CPU performance combined with average database operations and Redis SET operations makes it a viable option for relational databases, caching layers, and text processing tasks. However, the weak large-block memory read bandwidth and low medium-model LLM prompt processing speed suggest it is less optimal for large-scale vector processing or memory-bound machine learning workloads.
